claim: A Gateway Load Balancer operates at the third layer of the OSI model, listens for all IP packets across all ports, and forwards traffic to its target group with the GENEVE protocol on port 6081.
question: Which protocol and port does a Gateway Load Balancer use to send traffic to its appliances?

values.display: third layer of the Open Systems Interconnection
values.spoken: layer three of the OSI model

evidence.quote: A Gateway Load Balancer operates at the third layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. It listens for all IP packets across all ports and forwards traffic to the target group that's specified in the listener rule, using the GENEVE protocol on port 6081.

claim: The Gateway Load Balancer interface MTU supports packets up to 8,500 bytes and drops larger packets; GENEVE encapsulation adds 68 bytes, so appliances need an MTU of at least 8,568 bytes.
question: What packet size does a Gateway Load Balancer support, and what MTU do appliances need?

values.spoken: eight thousand five hundred sixty-eight bytes

evidence.quote: The Gateway Load Balancer interface MTU supports packets up to 8,500 bytes. Packets with a size larger than 8500 bytes that arrive at the Gateway Load Balancer interface are dropped.

The GENEVE encapsulation process adds 68 bytes to the original packet. Therefore, to support packets up to 8,500 bytes, ensure that the MTU setting of your appliance supports packets of at least 8,568 bytes.

claim: An Application Load Balancer functions at the application layer, the seventh layer of the OSI model, and evaluates listener rules in priority order to choose a target group.
question: At which OSI layer does an Application Load Balancer work?

values.display: the seventh layer of the Open Systems Interconnection
values.spoken: layer seven of the OSI model

evidence.quote: An Application Load Balancer functions at the application layer, the seventh layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. After the load balancer receives a request, it evaluates the listener rules in priority order to determine which rule to apply, and then selects a target from the target group for the rule action.
